reason: Both replies cover much the same ground (name a consequence, resolve the private-versus-public contradiction, fix the emergency line, add a real case), but B is more tied to these facts. B links the June 6–8 week promise to the August outage and adds the one-day-in-eight figure, which directly challenge the manager's belief that the outages were handled well. B also flags lines the association may not be able to back up, moves the second-elevator ask (where management may be right) down the list, and notes the draft is over length. A's 'give them something easy to agree to' is a good point for this reader, but its other advice is more generic.
